reference_items.native_verdict: consumed on the audio path; no entity-side consumer
reference_items.justification: The ambience model IS consumed on the audio path -- AmbienceDriver is stepped every frame from Engine._afterStep and renderBedOffline turns it into PCM out of which I measured 413 real events at HEAD -- so this is not the failure RI-MTH07 was written for, and round 1's genuine instance of that failure (R7 emitters unreachable) has been fixed. What it has no consumer for is the world: perturbing the model on 177 fields to inaudibility leaves every state hash, entity position and stealth alert value over a 3600-frame run with 89 entities BYTE-IDENTICAL to the null arm, while a positive control on the stealth detection sound-radius table diverges at the first sample. The builder's own consumption evidence does not demonstrate consumption at all: it perturbs the bed and measures spectral distance in the render, which is the audio model measuring itself. Marked down for that circularity and for the sterility, not zeroed, because the doctrine's 'entity changes behaviour' test is the wrong instrument for a subsystem whose output is sound.

ar1_souls_leakage.note: Nothing in a synthesised ambience bed carries a Morrowind combat mechanic. No roll-to-hit, no dice, no pause, no level scaling is reachable from this subsystem.

ar2_morrowind_leakage.note: No objective marker, bonfire warp, procedural loot or soul-currency purchase is expressed through the ambience layer.

ar3_seam_sterility.justification: The ambience model carries no boundary-crossing interaction. It is driven BY the world (region, position, time of day, weather are written into the driver from _afterStep) and read back only by instruments. Nothing a faction rank, a disposition, a quest resolution or a lore fact does changes what a region sounds like, and nothing a region sounds like changes what any entity does. This is the same finding as CONSUMPTION below, seen from the seam side: the subsystem is a leaf in both directions.

consumption.world_side_consumer: AmbienceDriver, constructed in the Engine constructor and stepped every frame from Engine._afterStep(); renderBedOffline() renders it to PCM. No consumer anywhere in game/src/sim/** or game/src/ai/** -- those trees contain zero references to ambience, and the perception model that does make entities behave differently because of sound (soundRadius in game/src/sim/stealth/detection.js) is a separate model reading separate data.
consumption.demonstrated_by_perturbation: 177 fields perturbed to inaudibility (every layer level_db to -60, every event_gain_db to 0, every event list emptied, every emitter removed, every bed_gain_db to -60). Over 3600 stepped frames with 89 entities and the player walking, all six state hashes, every entity position and every stealth alert value were IDENTICAL to the null arm. The null arm re-run after the destructive arm reproduced the first null exactly, so the null result is not an artefact of a broken teardown.
consumption.positive_control: The stealth detection sound-radius table scaled x8 (21 fields) diverges from the null arm at the FIRST sample and stays diverged. Without this the no-consumer reading would have been inadmissible, and the probe is written to exit 2 and say so.

biggest_gap.what: RI-AUD03 §A's 'Level (rel. bed)' band is a claim about EVENTS, and every mechanism that touches it is a per-layer median: gate O3 grades the median of a bed/layer's events, and the corrective trim `event_gain_db` is a single number per layer, while the second gain stage it corrects (`synth.gain_db`, -5..-13) varies PER EVENT. A per-layer trim cannot in principle unbury an event quieter than its layer-mates; it can only move the whole spread. The result is that the round-1 defect this piece exists to close -- declared in band, buried by a second gain stage -- is still present for individual events while the gate reports zero failures: 54 of 413 measured events sit outside §A's band with the tool's own +/-2 dB tolerance, 33 of them buried below the floor, in 11 of 33 bed/layer pairs whose median passes.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: The buried events are not marginal ones. blackwood/L3/distant_axe renders at -23.1 dB relative to the bed -- 15 dB below §A's floor -- and 'distant axe-strokes' is one of the three sounds that bed's own `brief` field advertises. deep-marshes/L3/marsh_gas_release reaches -30.4 dB. well/L3/stone_shift -16.3, dungeon/L3/block_settle -11.1. From the player's chair those sounds do not exist, which is exactly the state the B2 judge described as 'nothing ever happens in any of them' and exactly the state this round was commissioned to end. Because the gate is green, no future round has a reason to look.

remedy.action: Gate O3 on EVERY measured event rather than on the layer median -- the check is already written and falsifiable at tools/audio/critic-w1-22-r2-bands.mjs B1, which goes red on the shipped tree, redder under --sabotage widen, and GREEN under --sabotage centre (every event collapsed onto its layer median), proving its reading is about the spread and not about the level. Then give the trim the same granularity as the stage it corrects: calibrate a per-EVENT gain rather than one `event_gain_db` per layer, since the quantity being corrected varies per event. Both halves are small and neither needs new engine code.
remedy.acceptance: Re-run `node tools/audio/critic-w1-22-r2-bands.mjs` at the fixing commit and require B1 to report 0 of N events outside RI-AUD03 SectionA's band, with `--sabotage widen` still red and `--sabotage centre` still green so the check is known to be live. Then re-run `node tools/analysis/ambience-onsets.mjs --seconds 180` and require O1, O2 AND O3 green together on the same render (rule 9), with O3 rewritten to grade every event rather than the layer median.
